method: Independent source and pinned-backend review, plus inspection of peer reproduction code/results and screenshot evidence. Browser reproductions were executed by peers, not rerun by this secondary reviewer.
severityMeaning: Priority of the bounded frontend repair; not evidence of a production incident or automatic hold on the approved static preview.

reviews.confirmed: Same-ID receipt with old all-user access passes fileChangeForIdSchema after restricted access was requested; onSuccess invalidates and closes despite unchanged readback.
reviews.notEstablished: No unauthorized access, disclosure or backend ACL bypass was exercised. Current backend normally returns persisted normalized ACL fields.
reviews.action: Compare returned viewerMode and normalized viewerUserIds to the request; preserve the dialog and show failure/uncertainty on mismatch. P1 is justified by false completion of a confidentiality restriction.

reviews.confirmed: Move accepts an old folder in a same-ID receipt and closes with unchanged readback.
reviews.notEstablished: No normal-backend folder mutation failure was demonstrated; current backend returns the normalized persisted folder.
reviews.action: Compare normalized returned folder to requested folder; retain the editor on mismatch and verify the targeted file identity.

reviews.confirmed: After a synthetic HTTP503 the same-ID delete button permits a second user-triggered request. There is no unknown-outcome reconciliation UI.
reviews.notEstablished: No automatic retry, duplicate resource deletion, actual lost completion or provider effect was demonstrated. Pinned backend marks the same attachment inaccessible before object deletion, retains delete_failed for retry and returns404 after the row is gone. Repeating this DELETE is not equivalent to replaying note creation.
reviews.action: Treat as bounded recovery/readback UX work; reconcile absence or pending/failed deletion before reporting the final outcome. Do not block deployment solely because a second same-ID request is possible.

reviews.confirmed: Note-create HTTP200 arbitrary body is accepted through z.unknown; editor closes and draft is discarded while the note list remains unchanged. Save/edit/approve/share/unshare use the same unchecked acknowledgement owner.
reviews.notEstablished: Only note creation was freshly reproduced. No live data loss, cross-client save, disclosure, unauthorized sharing or provider effect was demonstrated.
reviews.action: Validate each action against its existing receipt: note/debrief metadata for save and approval, decorated meeting for share/unshare. Compare known scope/identity and preserve the draft on invalid receipt. Do not require plaintext body in encrypted-write metadata.

reviews.confirmed: A second user click after synthetic503 sends another note-creation POST. Source has no attempt token or unknown-outcome fence. Current backend calls meetingNote.create/meetingDebrief.create for each authorized request without request-level deduplication.
reviews.notEstablished: No actual duplicated database records were created. The synchronous double-submit subcase dispatches programmatic DOM events, so it proves lack of a handler guard rather than ordinary double-click behavior. Debrief follows shared source but was not separately exercised.
reviews.action: Add a synchronous single-dispatch guard and retain uncertain creation state for reconciliation; backend idempotency is useful additional protection. A simple rendered disabled button alone does not settle post-response-loss replay.

reviews.confirmed: Clearing Location or join URL omits location. Pinned backend preserves omitted location but clears an explicitly supplied empty value.
reviews.notEstablished: The combined fixture also returns a foreign receipt; source and backend semantics independently establish the omission problem without requiring that malformed receipt.
reviews.action: Send the explicit cleared value on edit and add an isolated clear/persist/readback case.

reviews.confirmed: Edit accepts a structurally valid receipt with a different meeting ID and client and closes. The shared creation branch also lacks comparison with submitted client context.
reviews.notEstablished: Fresh browser proof covers edit only; no cross-client native mutation, authorization bypass or exposure was demonstrated. Structural acceptance of an injected response alone does not establish those effects.
reviews.action: For edits validate original meeting ID and expected client; for creates validate selected client and a valid created identity. Preserve form state on mismatch. Add a create-specific mismatch proof before MCAL-007 acceptance. P2 matches the proven bounded false-completion behavior absent stronger impact evidence.

deploymentConclusion: CP-01/02 and CR-01–04 are actionable within existing frontend contracts. CP-03 warrants narrowed recovery wording and lower priority; current deletion contract already supports same-resource recovery. None of these synthetic probes proves a native privacy incident or provider side effect. Approved 4a image and source remain unchanged.
